lines.trans: Good night, team! I refilled Mei's two big white jars so everything looks tidy for dawn!
Wait, Manager Zhou—those two white ceramic jars had little paper labels underneath!
Oh, the paper got damp when I wiped the counter, so I threw both labels away.
Tell me both jars held sugar, boss. Please tell me both were sugar.
No, one bag was fine white caster sugar and one bag was fine white sea salt!
Which jar got the sugar, Manager Zhou—the left jar or the right jar?!
Left! Definitely left! ... Or did I turn both jars around when I polished the lids?
If Qing whisks four spoons of sea salt into Wednesday's lemon tarts, the city clerk will run!
Don't panic—tomorrow at six we taste a tiny pinch on a clean spoon before baking!
Write a big red note right now, Qing! Wait—who is knocking at the front gate at ten at night?!
Look through the lobby window—a woman in a blue coat holding a city folder?!
Wait—isn't the city clerk supposed to come Wednesday at three, NOT Tuesday night?!

meanings.note: Pinyin: yī. Changes tone to yí before 4th tone (一个 yí gè) and yì before 1st/2nd/3rd tones (一杯 yì bēi).

examples.text: 第一天上班，我走得快。电脑在哪里？
examples.trans: On my first day at work, I walk fast. Where is the computer?

examples.text: 第一条规矩：先喝热茶，再去开门。
examples.trans: Rule number one: drink hot tea first, then go answer the door.

meanings.en: a tiny bit; just a little
meanings.note: Pinyin: yì dián diǎn. Affectionate reduplication stressing how small an amount is.

examples.text: 只有一点点牛奶、两个鸡蛋，一点黄油都没有！
examples.trans: Only a tiny bit of milk, two eggs, and no butter at all!

examples.text: 我的红茶里只加一点点蜂蜜就够了。
examples.trans: Just a tiny bit of honey in my black tea is plenty.

meanings.note: Pinyin: sān. Cardinal number 3; combines with measure words (三个) and floors (三楼).

examples.text: 不在，只有我的笔和三张旧收据！
examples.trans: Not there—only my pen and three old receipts!

examples.text: 三瓶牛奶、二十个鸡蛋、黄油、奶酪和红苹果！
examples.trans: Three bottles of milk, twenty eggs, butter, cheese, and red apples!

meanings.note: Pinyin: xià wǔ. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 一个下午 ('an afternoon').

examples.text: 您尽管看，宋老师。星期一下午大堂暗。
examples.trans: Go right ahead, Teacher Song. Monday afternoon the lobby was dim.

examples.text: 先别对外面透露一个字！让两兄弟先过完这个星期五下午！
examples.trans: Not a single word to anyone outside yet! Let the two brothers have their Friday afternoon first!

meanings.note: Friendly farewell xiàcì jiàn.

examples.text: 今天聊得很开心，下次见！
examples.trans: Great chatting today, see you next time!

examples.text: 我们下次见！
examples.trans: See you next time!

meanings.note: Pinyin: bú duì. Negated adjective 不 ('not', shifting to 2nd-tone bú before 4th-tone duì) + 对 ('right/correct'); often used mid-sentence for a sudden realization ('wait, no!').

examples.text: 左边是糖……不对，もしかしたら右边那罐才是白糖？
examples.trans: The left jar is sugar... wait, no, could the right jar be the sugar?

examples.text: 老陈听了一下琴声说：“不对，这根弦还差一点点。”
examples.trans: Chen listened to the piano and said, 'Hold on, this string is still slightly off.'

meanings.note: Pinyin: bú shì. In 不是……吗？, forms a rhetorical question ('didn't you...? / isn't it...?'); bù shifts to bú before 4th-tone shì.

examples.text: 你不是说今天下午要去集市吗？
examples.trans: Didn't you say you were going to the market this afternoon?

examples.text: 那把钥匙不是一直放在抽屉里吗？
examples.trans: Hasn't that key been in the drawer all along?

meanings.note: Pinyin: liǎng. Used instead of 二 when counting things with a measure word (两个, 两把, 两间).

examples.text: 那是什么铃声？有人按了两下！
examples.trans: What was that bell sound? Somebody rang twice!

examples.text: 就算四号房空着，旧电线也会响两下。
examples.trans: Even when room four is empty, the old wire still rings twice.

meanings.note: Pinyin: gè. Most common Mandarin measure word (量词), placed between a number/demonstrative and a noun (一个人, 这个).

examples.text: 在抽屉里。我们这儿用这个大纸本子和铅笔。
examples.trans: In the drawer. Here we use this big paper ledger and a pencil.

examples.text: 刚烤好的面包卷！趁热拿一个吧。
examples.trans: Freshly baked bread rolls! Take one while it is hot.

meanings.note: Pinyin: zhī qián. Measure word (量词): 段, e.g. 那之前 ('before that time').

examples.text: 好。端上去之前，在上面撒这些新鲜绿香草。
examples.trans: Good. Before serving them, sprinkle these fresh green herbs on top.

examples.text: 先生，上楼之前，我要诚恳跟您道个歉。
examples.trans: Sir, before going upstairs, I owe you an honest apology.

meanings.note: Pinyin: le. After a verb, marks completion; at the end of a sentence, signals a change of situation.

examples.text: 早上好！请问，门锁了吗？
examples.trans: Good morning! Excuse me, is the door locked?

examples.text: 啊，开了！谢谢。我是小晴，新来的前台。
examples.trans: Oh, it opened! Thank you. I am Qing, the new receptionist.

meanings.note: Pinyin: wèi. Polite counterpart of 个 when counting guests, customers, or teachers (一位客人, 这位老师).

examples.text: 太谢谢你们两位了。
examples.trans: Thank you both so very much.

examples.text: 七点半有八位饿肚子的客人下楼啊！
examples.trans: At seven thirty, eight hungry guests are coming downstairs!

meanings.note: Pinyin: liù. Cardinal number 6.

examples.text: 老陈……小晴……快告诉我今晚六号房空着。
examples.trans: Chen... Qing... please tell me room six is free tonight.

examples.text: 没有啊，周经理，南方来的夫妻一小时前住进六号房了。
examples.trans: No, Manager Zhou, the couple from the south checked into room six an hour ago.

meanings.note: Pinyin: xiě. Used for writing characters, notes, letters, or reviews.

examples.text: 到星期五？没写名字，也没签名！
examples.trans: Until Friday? No name written, and no signature either!

examples.text: 只剩三十五分钟了！他肯定会写一星差评！
examples.trans: Only thirty-five minutes left! He will surely write a one-star bad review!

meanings.note: Pinyin: bié. Most commonly means 'do not' in polite commands (别担心 'don't worry'); as a verb, 'pin/clip on'.

examples.text: 谁也别说出去！门铃响的时候要微笑。
examples.trans: Do not tell anyone! Smile warmly when the bell rings.

examples.text: 您先坐下，别着急，我们马上看行李牌。
examples.trans: Please sit down first and do not worry; we will check the luggage tag right away.

meanings.note: Pinyin: qián mén. Combines 前 ('front') + 门 ('door/gate'); contrasts with 后门 ('back door'); measure word: 扇 (shàn).

examples.text: 都已经晚上十点了，是谁在敲我们小院的前门呀？
examples.trans: It is already ten o'clock at night—who could be knocking at our front gate?

examples.text: 每天早上七点，老陈都会准时打开客栈的前门迎接客人。
examples.trans: Every morning at seven sharp, Chen opens the front gate of the inn to welcome guests.

meanings.note: Pinyin: bàn shì yuán. Combines 办事 ('handle official business') + agent suffix 员 ('staff member').

examples.text: 市政厅的办事员星期三下午三点过来检查。
examples.trans: The city hall clerk is coming over at three on Wednesday afternoon to inspect.

examples.text: 窗口的办事员耐心地帮我们填好了表格。
examples.trans: The clerk at the counter patiently helped us fill out the form.

meanings.note: Pinyin: sháo. Used both as a noun (勺子 'spoon') and as a measure word for spoonfuls (一勺蜂蜜 'a spoonful of honey').

examples.text: 喝热柠檬茶的时候，加一勺蜂蜜最香。
examples.trans: Hot lemon tea smells best when you add a spoonful of honey.

examples.text: 请给我拿一把干净的小木勺。
examples.trans: Please bring me a clean little wooden spoon.

meanings.note: Pinyin: sháo zi. Measure word (量词): 把 (bǎ), e.g. 一把勺子 ('a spoon').

examples.text: 小勺子和餐巾放在哪里？
examples.trans: Where do the small spoons and napkins go?

examples.text: 每个蓝杯子旁边放一张餐巾和一把小勺子。
examples.trans: Beside every blue cup, put one napkin and one small spoon.

meanings.note: Pinyin: shí. Cardinal number 10; building block for 11–99.

examples.text: 我叫老陈。你早到了十分钟。
examples.trans: I'm called Chen. You arrived ten minutes early.

examples.text: 给您四号钥匙。早餐从七点半到十点。
examples.trans: Here is key number four for you. Breakfast is from seven thirty to ten.

meanings.note: Determiner lìng ('other, another').

examples.text: 另一个人说必须先私下向他道歉。
examples.trans: The other person insists on a private apology first.

examples.text: 我们还需要另外准备一套方案。
examples.trans: We need to prepare another backup plan.

meanings.note: In 推到台面上, means bringing a proposal into formal view.

examples.text: 他把这个方案推到了台面上。
examples.trans: He put this proposal openly on the table.

examples.text: 有些问题应该摆到台面上谈。
examples.trans: Some issues should be placed on the table and discussed openly.

meanings.note: Pinyin: yòu bian. Measure word (量词): 边 (biān), e.g. 右边 ('the right side').

examples.text: 这面圆镜子挂哪儿？窗户左边还是右边？
examples.trans: Where should I hang this round mirror? Left of the window or right?

examples.text: 挂在书桌右边吧，那里光线好。
examples.trans: Hang it to the right of the desk, where the light is good.

meanings.note: Pinyin: ma. Placed at the end of any statement to turn it into a neutral yes/no question.

examples.text: 早上好！请问，门锁了吗？
examples.trans: Good morning! Excuse me, is the door locked?

examples.text: 纸本子？真的吗？
examples.trans: A paper notebook? Really?

meanings.note: Pinyin: ya. Gentle exclamation of surprise or realization.

examples.text: 因为好咖啡和热面包让人开心呀！
examples.trans: Because good coffee and warm bread make people happy!

examples.text: 呀，这就是星期一火车上那只双胞胎箱子吗？
examples.trans: Oh, is this that twin suitcase from Monday's train?

meanings.note: Pinyin: gào su. Takes a person directly followed by the information (告诉我 'tell me').

examples.text: 太好了。请告诉我需要知道什么。
examples.trans: Great. Please tell me what I need to know.

examples.text: 告诉他们，我箱子上面口袋里有红丝带！
examples.trans: Tell them there is a red ribbon inside the top pocket of my case!

meanings.note: Pinyin: ne. After a noun, asks 'what about X?' (你呢？); at the end of a statement, highlights an ongoing situation.

examples.text: 等一下，咖啡厅的小美正朝我招手呢！
examples.trans: Wait a moment—Mei in the café is waving toward me right now!

examples.text: 来成都的第一个晚上，怎么能难过呢！
examples.trans: On your very first evening in Chengdu, how could you sit around sad!

meanings.note: Pinyin: ò. Signals realization or acknowledgment.

examples.text: 哦？我的预订有问题吗？
examples.trans: Oh? Is there a problem with my booking?

examples.text: 我？哦，我只是喜欢准时！七点十四分真美妙！
examples.trans: Me? Oh, I simply love punctuality! Seven fourteen is a lovely minute!

meanings.note: Pinyin: nǎ. Combines with a measure word to ask 'which?' (哪个 'which one?', 哪间 'which room?').

examples.text: 等一下，小晴……你拿了哪一包黄油？
examples.trans: Wait a second, Qing... which packet of butter did you grab?

examples.text: 对！左边有两条小路——我走哪一条？
examples.trans: Yes! There are two small lanes on the left—which one do I take?

meanings.note: Pinyin: sì. Cardinal number 4.

examples.text: 对，八间客房，八把铜钥匙。四号房的客人今天到。
examples.trans: Yes, eight rooms, eight brass keys. Room four's guest arrives today.

examples.text: 那里没人。那是四号房的门铃。
examples.trans: Nobody is there. That is the buzzer from room four.

meanings.note: Pinyin: zài. As main verb/preposition, gives location (在院子里); before another verb, marks ongoing action ('be doing').

examples.text: 第一天上班，我走得快。电脑在哪里？
examples.trans: On my first day at work, I walk fast. Where is the computer?

examples.text: 在抽屉里。我们这儿用这个大纸本子和铅笔。
examples.trans: In the drawer. Here we use this big paper ledger and a pencil.

meanings.note: Pinyin: dà. Everyday adjective for size, age, and strong wind or rain.

examples.text: 在抽屉里。我们这儿用这个大纸本子和铅笔。
examples.trans: In the drawer. Here we use this big paper ledger and a pencil.

examples.text: 两双棕色大男鞋，还有灰色毛衣。
examples.trans: Two pairs of big brown men's shoes, plus grey sweaters.

meanings.en: lobby; main hall (of an inn or hotel)
meanings.note: Pinyin: dà táng. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 一个大堂 ('a lobby').

examples.text: 满分十分给九分？！没人会去测量庭院，除非……
examples.trans: Nine out of ten?! Nobody measures courtyards unless...

examples.text: 您尽管看，宋老师。星期一下午大堂暗。
examples.trans: Go right ahead, Teacher Song. Monday afternoon the lobby was dim.

meanings.note: Pinyin: dà jiā. Warm collective pronoun including everyone in the group.

examples.text: 大家早上好！欢迎你，小晴。都准备好了吗？
examples.trans: Good morning, everyone! Welcome, Qing. Is everything ready?

examples.text: 有进步！今天小院迎接兄弟重逢——大家保持安静端庄！
examples.trans: Progress! Today our courtyard hosts a brotherly reunion—quiet dignity from everyone!

meanings.note: Pinyin: dà yī. Combines 大 ('large/outer') + 衣 ('garment/coat'); measure word: 件 (jiàn); verb: 穿 (chuān).

examples.text: 周经理站在院子外面的毛毛雨里，连大衣都忘了穿！
examples.trans: Manager Zhou is standing outside in the courtyard drizzle and even forgot to put on his coat!

examples.text: 雨天出门的时候记得穿上一件保暖的厚大衣。
examples.trans: Remember to put on a warm overcoat when heading out in the rain.

meanings.note: Pinyin: nǚ shì. Measure word (量词): 位 (wèi), e.g. 一位女士 ('a lady').

examples.text: 打扰了，女士……等等，这个声音！教钢琴的宋老师？！
examples.trans: Excuse me, ma'am... wait, that voice! Teacher Song, my piano teacher?!

examples.text: 前台有位姓宋的女士在等您。
examples.trans: A Ms. Song is waiting for you at reception.

meanings.note: Pinyin: xiǎo. Everyday adjective for small size; also prefixes younger colleagues' names warmly (小晴, 小美).

examples.text: 早上好，姑娘。我有一个宋名下的预订。
examples.trans: Good morning, young lady. I have a booking for Song.

examples.text: 白纸包着什么？一个木头小火车！
examples.trans: What is wrapped in white paper? A little wooden train!

meanings.note: Pinyin: cháng chang. Softened reduplication of 尝 ('taste'), standard when inviting someone to sample food.

examples.text: 快来尝尝我刚烤出来的杏仁柠檬挞！
examples.trans: Come have a taste of the almond lemon tart I just baked!

examples.text: 你先尝尝这碗番茄汤咸淡合适不合适。
examples.trans: Have a taste of this tomato soup first to see if the seasoning is right.

meanings.note: Pinyin: jiù. Highlights immediacy, exact location (就在这里), or smooth consequence ('then').

examples.text: 就在您额头上，安全得很。
examples.trans: Right there on your forehead, completely safe.

examples.text: 朝院子，就在老树上面，非常安静。
examples.trans: Toward the courtyard, right above the old tree; it is very quiet.

meanings.note: Pinyin: zuǒ bian. Measure word (量词): 边 (biān), e.g. 左边 ('the left side').

examples.text: 这面圆镜子挂哪儿？窗户左边还是右边？
examples.trans: Where should I hang this round mirror? Left of the window or right?

examples.text: 对！左边有两条小路——我走哪一条？
examples.trans: Yes! There are two small lanes on the left—which one do I take?

meanings.note: Pinyin: shì zhèng tīng. Measure word (量词): 座 (zuò), e.g. 一座市政厅 ('a city hall').

examples.text: 等等，志鹏——你还在市政厅合同科工作？！
examples.trans: Wait, Zhipeng—you still work at City Hall's contract office?!

examples.text: 下周我保证把半个市政厅的同事都带来小美这儿喝咖啡。
examples.trans: Next week I promise to bring half my City Hall colleagues to Mei's tables.

meanings.note: Pinyin: gān jìng. Note first tone gān ('dry/clean'), never fourth tone.

examples.text: 周经理早！桌子很干净，钥匙也准备好了。
examples.trans: Morning, Manager Zhou! The desk is clean, and the keys are ready too.

examples.text: 放心吧，周经理。房间干净，毛巾也是新的。
examples.trans: Relax, Manager Zhou. The room is clean, and the towels are fresh.

meanings.note: Pinyin: dǐ xia. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 最底下 ('the bottom').

examples.text: 看车轮底下——铅笔写的你和我的名字还在那儿。
examples.trans: Look underneath the wheels—your name and mine in pencil are still right there.

examples.text: 前面锁扣有个小锁孔，再看底下贴着：一把旧铜钥匙！
examples.trans: There is a tiny keyhole on the front latch, and taped underneath: an old brass key!

张.gloss: measure word for flat surfaces and paper

meanings.en: measure word for flat surfaces and paper
meanings.note: Pinyin: zhāng. Counts tables, beds, paper sheets, tickets, receipts, and luggage tags (一张桌子, 一张纸).

examples.text: 不在，只有我的笔和三张旧收据！
examples.trans: Not there—only my pen and three old receipts!

examples.text: 旁边的把手上系着一张小纸牌。
examples.trans: There is a small paper card tied on the side handle.

meanings.note: Pinyin: wǎng. Guides movement in directions (往上提 'lift upward', 往左拐 'turn left').

examples.text: 早上好。没锁，先把把手往上提，再推。
examples.trans: Good morning. Not locked; lift the handle up first, then push.

examples.text: 从这儿往里走。我帮您把蓝色行李箱提上去。
examples.trans: Walk inward from here. I will carry the blue suitcase up for you.

meanings.note: Pinyin: kuài. As an adjective/adverb, 'fast/quickly'; in 快…了, 'about to'.

examples.text: 第一天上班，我走得快。电脑在哪里？
examples.trans: On my first day at work, I walk fast. Where is the computer?

examples.text: 小晴，快看里面！这不是我的箱子！
examples.trans: Qing, look inside quickly! This is not my case!

meanings.note: Pinyin: zěn me. Before a verb, asks 'how to do X?' (怎么走) or 'how come…?' (怎么还没来).

examples.text: 我的眼镜怎么会在……哎呀！在我头上！
examples.trans: Why would my glasses be in... oh dear! They are on my head!

examples.text: 宋老师，怎么了？您按了门铃！
examples.trans: Teacher Song, what happened? You rang the bell!

meanings.note: Pinyin: nín. Respectful singular 'you' used with elders, teachers, and guests (您好！).

examples.text: 在您的外套口袋里吗？
examples.trans: Are they in your coat pocket?

examples.text: 就在您额头上，安全得很。
examples.trans: Right there on your forehead, completely safe.

meanings.note: Pinyin: huāng. Describes feeling rattled or panicked (别慌 'don't panic').

examples.text: 等周经理听说他为分贝慌了一整夜，表情一定精彩！
examples.trans: Wait until Manager Zhou hears he panicked all night over decibels!

examples.text: 对。我一慌，按了门铃，把星期五纸条贴在把手上。
examples.trans: Yes. In a panic I rang the bell and taped the Friday note onto the handle.

meanings.note: Pinyin: wǒ. First-person singular pronoun; add 的 for 'my' (我的) and 们 for 'we/us' (我们).

examples.text: 啊，开了！谢谢。我是小晴，新来的前台。
examples.trans: Oh, it opened! Thank you. I am Qing, the new receptionist.

examples.text: 我叫老陈。你早到了十分钟。
examples.trans: I'm called Chen. You arrived ten minutes early.

meanings.note: Pinyin: wǒ men. First-person plural pronoun; add 的 for 'our' (我们的).

examples.text: 在抽屉里。我们这儿用这个大纸本子和铅笔。
examples.trans: In the drawer. Here we use this big paper ledger and a pencil.

examples.text: 谢谢！我们平时都直接叫名字吗？
examples.trans: Thank you! Do we usually just call each other by name here?

meanings.note: Pinyin: cái. Signals that something happened later than expected or in a small amount—contrast 就.

examples.text: 老砖房顶楼平时要等很久水才热。
examples.trans: Top floors in old brick houses usually wait ages before the water warms up.

examples.text: 因为房子只是砖头和木头，志鹏，家人才是留住的东西。
examples.trans: Because a house is only brick and timber, Zhipeng—family is what we keep.

meanings.note: Pinyin: rēng diào. Resultative verb compound 扔 ('throw/toss') + 掉 ('away/off').

examples.text: 周经理擦台面的时候纸标签湿了，就把两张标签都扔掉了。
examples.trans: When Manager Zhou wiped the counter, the paper labels got damp, so he threw both of them away.

examples.text: 旧木箱里那些生锈断掉的钉子已经被老陈扔掉了。
examples.trans: The rusty broken nails inside the old wooden chest have already been thrown away by Chen.

meanings.en: measure word for handled objects; disposal marker
meanings.note: Pinyin: bǎ. Counts items with handles or backs (一把钥匙, 一把椅子); as a preposition, fronts a definite object before an action verb.

examples.text: 早上好。没锁，先把把手往上提，再推。
examples.trans: Good morning. Not locked; lift the handle up first, then push.

examples.text: 对，八间客房，八把铜钥匙。四号房的客人今天到。
examples.trans: Yes, eight rooms, eight brass keys. Room four's guest arrives today.

拔腿就跑.gloss: take to one's heels; bolt right off

meanings.en: take to one's heels; bolt right off
meanings.note: Pinyin: bá tuǐ jiù pǎo. Vivid four-character phrase 拔腿 ('pull up one's legs') + 就跑 ('and run right off').

examples.text: 周经理一听说罐子没贴标签，抓起围裙拔腿就跑去拿新纸条了！
examples.trans: The moment Manager Zhou heard the jars had no labels, he grabbed his apron and bolted off to get fresh paper slips!

examples.text: 小猫听见院子门口的铃声，吓得拔腿就跑进了花丛里。
examples.trans: Hearing the bell at the courtyard gate, the kitten bolted into the flower bushes.

meanings.note: Pinyin: ná. Core verb for holding or fetching objects in the hand.

examples.text: 刚烤好的面包卷！趁热拿一个吧。
examples.trans: Freshly baked bread rolls! Take one while it is hot.

examples.text: 火车站有人拿错了我的蓝色行李箱！
examples.trans: Someone at the train station took my blue suitcase by mistake!

related.gloss: handle with care (lift gently, set down gently)

meanings.note: Pinyin: niē. Action verb for picking up a tiny pinch of salt/sugar with the fingers or shaping dough by hand.

examples.text: 明天早上六点烤点心以前，我们先捏一点点白粉末尝尝就行。
examples.trans: Tomorrow morning at six before baking, we can just pinch a tiny bit of the white powder to taste.

examples.text: 小美教志鹏怎么用手指把杏仁挞皮的边缘捏出漂亮的花纹。
examples.trans: Mei showed Peng how to pinch a neat fluted pattern around the edge of the almond tart shells.

meanings.note: Pinyin: jiǎo. Action verb for stirring liquids, sauces, or batters with a spoon or whisk.

examples.text: 小晴开着小火不停地搅，不让锅底的柠檬酱煮开。
examples.trans: Qing stirred nonstop over low heat so the lemon curd at the bottom of the pot wouldn't boil.

examples.text: 喝热红茶的时候，他喜欢放一小勺蜂蜜轻轻搅一下。
examples.trans: When drinking hot black tea, he likes adding a small spoonful of honey and giving it a gentle stir.

meanings.note: Pinyin: cā. Used for wiping tables, drying water, or polishing lanterns.

examples.text: 别担心！用冰气泡水一擦，橙汁就掉。
examples.trans: Do not worry! Wipe it once with cold sparkling water and orange juice comes right out.

examples.text: 先生，给您干毛巾擦外套，还有一碗热汤。
examples.trans: Sir, here is a dry towel to wipe your coat, plus a bowl of hot soup.

meanings.note: Pinyin: qiāo. Used for knocking on doors or pipes clanking.

examples.text: 听……街口钟楼开始敲十二下了！
examples.trans: Listen... the clock tower at the end of the street is starting to strike twelve!

examples.text: 十二下敲完了……大门外面街上空荡荡的。
examples.trans: Twelve chimes have finished... and the street outside the gate is completely empty.

meanings.note: Pinyin: zhěng zhěng qí qí. AABB reduplication of 整齐 ('neat/orderly'), often followed by 地 before verbs or 的 before nouns.

examples.text: 十二个白茶杯整整齐齐地摆在木托盘上。
examples.trans: Twelve white teacups are lined up neatly on the wooden tray.

examples.text: 小晴把前台的账本和钥匙收得整整齐齐。
examples.trans: Qing tidied up the front-desk ledgers and keys in neat order.

meanings.note: Pinyin: wén jiàn jiā. Combines 文件 ('document/file') + 夹 ('clip/folder'); measure word: 个 (gè).

examples.text: 门外站着一个人，手里还拿着一个正式的文件夹呢！
examples.trans: Someone is standing outside the front gate holding an official file folder!

examples.text: 周经理把市政厅寄来的审核清单整齐地收进了蓝色文件夹里。
examples.trans: Manager Zhou filed the review checklist from City Hall neatly inside a blue folder.

meanings.note: Pinyin: zǎo shang. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 一个早上 ('a morning').

examples.text: 早上好！请问，门锁了吗？
examples.trans: Good morning! Excuse me, is the door locked?

examples.text: 早上好。没锁，先把把手往上提，再推。
examples.trans: Good morning. Not locked; lift the handle up first, then push.

meanings.note: Pinyin: míng tiān. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 明天一天 ('all day tomorrow').

examples.text: 欢迎来到小院客栈，小晴。明天不会无聊了。
examples.trans: Welcome to Courtyard Inn, Qing. Tomorrow will not be boring.

examples.text: 晚安，小晴。明天早餐见。
examples.trans: Good night, Qing. See you at breakfast tomorrow.

meanings.note: Pinyin: míng zǎo. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 明天早上 ('tomorrow morning').

examples.text: 定好闹钟吧，老陈。明早我们跑赢冷水！
examples.trans: Set your alarm, Chen. Tomorrow morning we outrun the cold water!

examples.text: 明早七点半我们在楼下咖啡馆见。
examples.trans: Let's meet downstairs in the café tomorrow morning at seven thirty.

meanings.note: Pinyin: xīng qī sān. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 这星期三 ('this Wednesday').

examples.text: 等等——星期三晚上你又用真名住进来了？
examples.trans: Wait—and Wednesday night you checked in here under your real name?

examples.text: 每到星期三下午，小美都会试烤新甜点。
examples.trans: Every Wednesday afternoon, Mei test-bakes a new pastry.

meanings.note: Pinyin: xīng qī èr. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 这星期二 ('this Tuesday').

examples.text: 老房子每到星期二就松一颗螺丝。坐吧。
examples.trans: Every Tuesday an old house loosens one screw. Sit down.

examples.text: 甚至星期二您还打电话提过白纸包的事！
examples.trans: Even after you called us on Tuesday about the white parcel!

meanings.note: Pinyin: shì. Links two nouns (我是小晴); do NOT use simple 是 before plain adjectives like 好 or 忙.

examples.text: 啊，开了！谢谢。我是小晴，新来的前台。
examples.trans: Oh, it opened! Thank you. I am Qing, the new receptionist.

examples.text: 有道理！这些是钥匙吗？
examples.trans: Fair enough! Are these the keys?

meanings.note: Pinyin: shì bú shì. A-not-A affirmative-negative question tag; bù shifts to bú before 4th-tone shì.

examples.text: 我们俩是不是刚升职当上正式试吃员了？
examples.trans: Did the two of us just get promoted to official taste testers?

examples.text: 你是不是把绿色登记本夹在胳膊底下了？
examples.trans: Didn't you tuck the green guest book under your arm?

meanings.note: Pinyin: wǎn shang. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 一个晚上 ('an evening').

examples.text: 来成都的第一个晚上，怎么能难过呢！
examples.trans: On your very first evening in Chengdu, how could you sit around sad!

examples.text: 晚上九点？等等，我们一起去开大门。
examples.trans: At nine o'clock? Wait, let us open the gate together.

meanings.note: Pinyin: wǎn ān. Warm bedtime greeting.

examples.text: 晚安，小晴。明天早餐见。
examples.trans: Good night, Qing. See you at breakfast tomorrow.

examples.text: 时间不早了，早点休息，晚安！
examples.trans: It is getting late—get some rest, good night!

meanings.note: Pinyin: lái. Movement toward the speaker, as main verb or directional complement (进来 'come in').

examples.text: 啊，开了！谢谢。我是小晴，新来的前台。
examples.trans: Oh, it opened! Thank you. I am Qing, the new receptionist.

examples.text: 大门口正好来了一辆出租车。
examples.trans: A taxi has just pulled up right at the front gate.

meanings.note: Pinyin: níng méng tà. Combines 柠檬 ('lemon') + 挞 ('tart', phonetic loan from English 'tart').

examples.text: 星期二我们要修好琴键，还要烤星期三的柠檬挞！
examples.trans: On Tuesday we will fix the piano key and bake Wednesday's lemon tarts!

examples.text: 酸甜清香的杏仁柠檬挞成了咖啡角的招牌甜点。
examples.trans: Sweet-tart, fragrant almond lemon tart became the café corner's signature dessert.

meanings.note: Pinyin: biāo qiān. Combines 标 ('mark/sign') + 签 ('inscribed slip/tag'); measure word: 张 (zhāng); verb: 贴标签 ('stick on a label').

examples.text: 睡觉以前，先把那两个神秘白罐子都贴上清楚的大红标签。
examples.trans: Before going to bed, stick clear bright red labels onto both of those mysterious white jars.

examples.text: 贴好“白糖”和“海盐”的标签以后，早上做点心就再也不会拿错了。
examples.trans: Once the 'Sugar' and 'Sea Salt' labels are stuck on, nobody will mix them up during morning baking.

meanings.note: Pinyin: qiú. Used for earnest requests (求你了 'please, I beg you!').

examples.text: 老陈，求你告诉我只是水管进了一点气！
examples.trans: Chen, please tell me it was just a tiny bit of air in the pipe!

examples.text: 我求他再给我们一天时间。
examples.trans: I pleaded with him to give us one more day.

meanings.note: Pinyin: hǎi yán. Measure word (量词): 撮, e.g. 一撮海盐 ('a pinch of sea salt').

examples.text: 那是海盐咸黄油！甜果酱面包卷要无盐黄油！
examples.trans: That is sea-salt butter! Sweet jam rolls need unsalted butter!

examples.text: 小晴买了海盐黄油，今天我们做嫩炒蛋！
examples.trans: Qing bought sea-salt butter, so today we are making soft scrambled eggs!

related.gloss: a pinch of sea salt (measure word 撮)

meanings.note: Pinyin: shī. Describes clothes, shoes, or streets wet from rain.

examples.text: 晚上好。不好意思，把干净地板弄湿了。
examples.trans: Good evening. Sorry for getting your clean floor wet.

examples.text: 因为湿木头百叶窗会柔化石板路传回来的回声……
examples.trans: Because wet wooden shutters soften the echo bouncing off the flagstones...

meanings.note: Pinyin: diǎn. Marks hours on the clock (八点 'eight o'clock') or 'a bit' (一点).

examples.text: 给您四号钥匙。早餐从七点半到十点。
examples.trans: Here is key number four for you. Breakfast is from seven thirty to ten.

examples.text: 晚上九点？等等，我们一起去开大门。
examples.trans: At nine o'clock? Wait, let us open the gate together.

meanings.note: Pinyin: kǎo. Used for baking bread, rolls, and cakes in an oven.

examples.text: 刚烤好的面包卷！趁热拿一个吧。
examples.trans: Freshly baked bread rolls! Take one while it is hot.

examples.text: 多烤几块边角，好姑娘！
examples.trans: Bake plenty of corner pieces, dear girl!

meanings.note: Pinyin: xiàn zài. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 现在这时候 ('this moment right now').

examples.text: 现在他的箱子还安全锁着呢。
examples.trans: For now, his suitcase stays safely locked up.

examples.text: 太好了！现在我想吃一顿丰盛的早餐。
examples.trans: Wonderful! Now I would like to eat a big breakfast.

related.gloss: this moment right now (measure word 个)

meanings.note: Pinyin: cí guàn. Combines 瓷 ('porcelain/ceramic') + 罐 ('jar/canister'); measure word: 个 (gè) or 只 (zhī).

examples.text: 那两个装白糖和海盐的白瓷罐底下原本贴着小纸标签呢！
examples.trans: Those two white ceramic jars holding sugar and sea salt originally had small paper labels stuck underneath!

examples.text: 把茶叶存放在密封的白瓷罐里，香气能保持很久。
examples.trans: Storing tea leaves in a sealed porcelain canister keeps their fragrance fresh for a long time.

meanings.note: Pinyin: yòng. Works as main verb ('use a key') or preposition ('with/using').

examples.text: 在抽屉里。我们这儿用这个大纸本子和铅笔。
examples.trans: In the drawer. Here we use this big paper ledger and a pencil.

examples.text: 别担心！用冰气泡水一擦，橙汁就掉。
examples.trans: Do not worry! Wipe it once with cold sparkling water and orange juice comes right out.

meanings.note: Pinyin: bái. Describes white paper, sugar, or tablecloths.

examples.text: 白纸包着什么？一个木头小火车！
examples.trans: What is wrapped in white paper? A little wooden train!

examples.text: 看，把手上贴着一个白信封。
examples.trans: Look, there is a white envelope taped onto the handle.

meanings.note: Pinyin: bái shā táng. Combines 白 ('white') + 砂 ('fine sand-like crystal grains') + 糖 ('sugar').

examples.text: 周经理说两个罐子里的东西看起来一模一样，都像白砂糖！
examples.trans: Manager Zhou said the contents of both jars looked identical—both looked just like white caster sugar!

examples.text: 烤杏仁挞底和熬柠檬酱都需要用到颗粒细小的白砂糖。
examples.trans: Both baking almond tart shells and cooking lemon curd call for fine-grained white caster sugar.

meanings.note: Pinyin: de. Links modifiers or owners to nouns (我的书 'my book', 安静的院子 'quiet courtyard').

examples.text: 啊，开了！谢谢。我是小晴，新来的前台。
examples.trans: Oh, it opened! Thank you. I am Qing, the new receptionist.

examples.text: 纸本子？真的吗？
examples.trans: A paper notebook? Really?

meanings.note: Pinyin: de shí hou. High-frequency temporal frame placed at the end of a verb or clause to mean 'when / while ...' (往下迈的时候 'when stepping down').

examples.text: 小美够最上面那层架子的时候，小晴赶紧上前扶住了木凳。
examples.trans: While Mei was reaching for the top shelf, Qing hurried over to steady the wooden stool.

examples.text: 我擦厨房台面的时候，罐子底下的纸标签不小心被水弄湿了。
examples.trans: When I was wiping the kitchen counter, the paper labels under the jars got damp.

meanings.note: Pinyin: gài zi. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 一个木头盖子 ('a wooden lid').

examples.text: 开了！老陈，快打开木头盖子！
examples.trans: It's open! Chen, quick, lift the wooden lid!

examples.text: 盖子要小心一点——它已经关了几十年了。
examples.trans: Careful with the lid—it has been closed for decades.

meanings.note: Pinyin: kàn. Covers looking at something, reading silently, or visiting someone; add 见/到 for 'catch sight of'.

examples.text: 我要看预订本子，可是找不到我的眼镜了！
examples.trans: I need to read the booking ledger, yet I cannot find my glasses!

examples.text: 老板，看一下桌子后面的镜子。
examples.trans: Boss, take a look in the mirror behind the desk.

meanings.note: Pinyin: zhe. Placed right after a verb to show a state or posture continues (门开着 'the door stands open').

examples.text: 就算四号房空着，旧电线也会响两下。
examples.trans: Even when room four is empty, the old wire still rings twice.

examples.text: 白纸包着什么？一个木头小火车！
examples.trans: What is wrapped in white paper? A little wooden train!

meanings.note: Pinyin: chuān. Used for garments and footwear that the body steps or slips into.

examples.text: 我可不穿四十四码的鞋！
examples.trans: I certainly do not wear size forty-four shoes!

examples.text: 宋老师，您穿着很合适。
examples.trans: Teacher Song, it fits you very well.

meanings.note: Pinyin: chuāng hu. Measure word (量词): 扇 (shàn), e.g. 一扇窗户 ('a window').

examples.text: 太好了。窗户朝街上还是朝院子？
examples.trans: Wonderful. Does the window face the street or the courtyard?

examples.text: 哇，看这间房！大木头房梁，窗户正对着院子！
examples.trans: Wow, look at this room! Big wooden beams, and a window facing the courtyard!

meanings.note: Pinyin: děng deng. Urgent or casual reduplication of 等 ('wait!').

examples.text: 等等，深蓝色的，跟您的一样啊！
examples.trans: Wait—it is dark blue, the same as yours!

examples.text: 等等，这条街就在附近，走过去只要五分钟！
examples.trans: Wait—that street is right nearby, only five minutes on foot!

meanings.note: Pinyin: táng. Measure word (量词): 块 (kuài), e.g. 一块糖 ('a piece of candy / sugar cube').

examples.text: 请给我不加糖的红茶，再来一片热面包。
examples.trans: Black tea without added sugar, please, and one slice of warm bread.

examples.text: 太好了！请加牛奶和一点糖。
examples.trans: Wonderful! With milk and a little sugar, please.

related.gloss: a piece of candy / sugar cube (measure word 块)

meanings.note: Pinyin: hóng. Describes the color red; note that 红茶 is what English calls 'black tea'.

examples.text: 告诉他们，我箱子上面口袋里有红丝带！
examples.trans: Tell them there is a red ribbon inside the top pocket of my case!

examples.text: 我的行李箱！快打开上面口袋……对，红丝带！
examples.trans: My suitcase! Let me open the top pocket... yes, the red ribbon!

meanings.note: Pinyin: zhǐ. Measure word (量词): 张 (zhāng), e.g. 一张纸 ('a sheet of paper').

examples.text: 在抽屉里。我们这儿用这个大纸本子和铅笔。
examples.trans: In the drawer. Here we use this big paper ledger and a pencil.

examples.text: 纸本子？真的吗？
examples.trans: A paper notebook? Really?

related.gloss: a sheet of paper (measure word 张)

meanings.en: slip of paper; short written note
meanings.note: Pinyin: zhǐ tiáo. Measure word (量词): 张 (zhāng), e.g. 一张纸条 ('a paper slip / note').

examples.text: 他留了纸条，请我们保管到星期五。
examples.trans: He left a note asking us to keep it until Friday.

examples.text: 对。我一慌，按了门铃，把星期五纸条贴在把手上。
examples.trans: Yes. In a panic I rang the bell and taped the Friday note onto the handle.

related.gloss: a paper slip / note (measure word 张)

meanings.note: Pinyin: xì. Describes slender tools (细镊子 'thin tweezers'), fine grit (细砂纸), or careful work.

examples.text: 明天早上给我一把细镊子和一点木工胶水就行。
examples.trans: Just give me thin tweezers and a little woodworking glue tomorrow morning.

examples.text: 春天的细雨轻轻落在院子的常春藤叶上。
examples.trans: Fine spring rain fell softly onto the ivy leaves in the courtyard.

罐.gloss: jar of; pot of; tin of

meanings.en: jar of; pot of; tin of
meanings.note: Pinyin: guàn. Serves both as a noun (罐子 'jar/crock') and as a measure word for jars or tins (两罐蜂蜜 'two jars of honey').

examples.text: 竹篮子里装着两罐沉甸甸的百花蜂蜜。
examples.trans: Packed inside the bamboo basket are two heavy jars of wildflower honey.

examples.text: 小美做了四小罐草莓果酱放在厨房架子上。
examples.trans: Mei made four small jars of strawberry jam and set them on the kitchen shelf.

meanings.note: Pinyin: guàn zi. Combines 罐 ('jar/pot/canister') + noun suffix 子; measure word: 个 (gè) or 只 (zhī).

examples.text: 厨房架子上整整齐齐摆着两个装白糖和海盐的白瓷罐子。
examples.trans: Two white ceramic jars holding sugar and sea salt sit neatly on the kitchen shelf.

examples.text: 小晴把刚烤好的杏仁饼干装进密封玻璃罐子里，防止受潮。
examples.trans: Qing packed the freshly baked almond biscuits into an airtight glass jar to keep them crisp.

meanings.note: Pinyin: láo bǎn. Measure word (量词): 位 (wèi), e.g. 一位老板 ('a boss / shop owner').

examples.text: 老板，看一下桌子后面的镜子。
examples.trans: Boss, take a look in the mirror behind the desk.

examples.text: 老板正在开锁呢！别挂电话，等我一秒钟。
examples.trans: The owner is unlocking it right now! Stay on the phone, wait one second.

related.gloss: a boss / shop owner (measure word 位)

meanings.note: Pinyin: kěn dìng. Colloquial cousin of 一定 for confident predictions.

examples.text: 箱子的主人肯定很快会来找的。
examples.trans: The suitcase's owner will surely come looking for it soon.

examples.text: 只剩三十五分钟了！他肯定会写一星差评！
examples.trans: Only thirty-five minutes left! He will surely write a one-star bad review!

meanings.note: Pinyin: lán. Describes blue suitcases, doors, or teacups.

examples.text: 每个蓝杯子旁边放一张餐巾和一把小勺子。
examples.trans: Beside every blue cup, put one napkin and one small spoon.

examples.text: 储藏室里有两个软枕头和一块蓝地毯！
examples.trans: In the storeroom there are two soft pillows and a blue rug!

meanings.note: Pinyin: xíng. Read xíng when meaning 'that works / okay' (不行 'won't work'); read háng when counting lines of text (第一行).

examples.text: 等等，咸黄油配果酱不行，做炒蛋却棒极了！
examples.trans: Wait—salted butter fails with jam, yet for scrambled eggs it is amazing!

examples.text: 小晴，替我念第一行。快说是我眼镜又看花眼了！
examples.trans: Qing, read the top line for me. Tell me my glasses are playing tricks on my eyes!

meanings.note: Classifier/noun dài ('bagful').

examples.text: 麻烦你们把这袋硬盘送回素材房。
examples.trans: Please carry this bag of hard drives back to the archive room.

examples.text: 她买了一袋新鲜苹果。
examples.trans: She bought a bag of fresh apples.

meanings.note: Pinyin: zhuāng. Used for packing items into a bag/box (装进) or fitting hardware.

examples.text: 我来帮您。哎呀，里面装了石头吗？
examples.trans: Let me help you. Goodness, did you pack stones inside?

examples.text: 他没要回那个装木头小火车的箱子吗？
examples.trans: Did he not ask back for that case with the wooden train?

meanings.note: Pinyin: zhuāng mǎn. Resultative verb compound 装 ('fill/load/hold') + 满 ('full').

examples.text: 这台老核桃木琴箱发出的温暖琴声，把整间玻璃房都装满了！
examples.trans: The warm sound from this old walnut piano case filled the entire glass room!

examples.text: 周经理睡觉以前把小美那两个大白瓷罐都装满了。
examples.trans: Before going to bed, Manager Zhou filled both of Mei's big white ceramic jars to the brim.

meanings.note: Pinyin: yào shi. Everyday spoken 'if', often paired with 就 in the main clause.

examples.text: 等等——要是每天早上打开院门，卖街坊咖啡和热面包……
examples.trans: Wait—if we open our courtyard gate every morning for neighbourhood coffee and warm bread...

examples.text: 周经理，要是你不正式聘用她，我就请她进我厨房！
examples.trans: Manager Zhou, if you do not hire her permanently, I am hiring her into my kitchen!

meanings.note: Pinyin: shuí. Question pronoun for people; stays in the exact spot of the answer (这是谁的？ 'Whose is this?').

examples.text: 谁也别说出去！门铃响的时候要微笑。
examples.trans: Do not tell anyone! Smile warmly when the bell rings.

examples.text: 一点没破！是谁送回来的？
examples.trans: Not cracked at all! Who brought it back?

meanings.note: Pinyin: tiē. Used for taping envelopes, labels, or notices onto a surface.

examples.text: 看，把手上贴着一个白信封。
examples.trans: Look, there is a white envelope taped onto the handle.

examples.text: 对。我一慌，按了门铃，把星期五纸条贴在把手上。
examples.trans: Yes. In a panic I rang the bell and taped the Friday note onto the handle.

meanings.note: Pinyin: zhuàn. Read zhuàn for spinning wheels or quick wits (脑子转得快 'mind works fast').

examples.text: 脑子转得快，小晴。志豪每星期都读城市建筑规定。
examples.trans: Quick thinking, Qing. Hao reads city building rules every single week.

examples.text: 风一吹，纸风车就飞快地转起来。
examples.trans: When the breeze blows, the paper pinwheel spins fast.

meanings.note: Pinyin: guò lái. Directional compound moving across toward the speaker.

examples.text: 你看，早餐忙乱和神秘电话你都挺过来了！
examples.trans: Look, you made it through both the breakfast rush and the mystery phone call!

examples.text: 因为星期一晚上我走过来时，看见我哥哥正走在这条街上！
examples.trans: Because when I walked here Monday night, I saw my older brother walking down this street!

meanings.note: Pinyin: hái shi. Joins choices in questions (茶还是咖啡？ 'tea or coffee?') or means 'still'.

examples.text: 太好了。窗户朝街上还是朝院子？
examples.trans: Wonderful. Does the window face the street or the courtyard?

examples.text: 宋老师早！您想喝咖啡还是红茶？
examples.trans: Morning, Teacher Song! Would you like coffee or black tea?

meanings.note: Pinyin: jìn. Movement into an enclosed space (请进 'come in!', 倒进 'pour into').

examples.text: 小晴，把热水倒进茶壶里，他们来了！
examples.trans: Qing, pour the hot water into the teapot—here they come!

examples.text: 没有啊，周经理，南方来的夫妻一小时前住进六号房了。
examples.trans: No, Manager Zhou, the couple from the south checked into room six an hour ago.

meanings.note: Pinyin: tòu guò. Describes light or sound passing through an opening.

examples.text: 哎呀！透过窗户看见周经理了？我明明加倍用力微笑了！
examples.trans: Oh dear! You spotted Manager Zhou through the window? I smiled twice as wide!

examples.text: 早晨的阳光透过树叶照在白桌布上。
examples.trans: Morning sunshine filters through the leaves onto the white tablecloth.

meanings.note: Pinyin: nà. Distal demonstrative before measure words (那个 'that one'); at clause start, means 'then / well then'.

examples.text: 那是什么铃声？有人按了两下！
examples.trans: What was that bell sound? Somebody rang twice!

examples.text: 那里没人。那是四号房的门铃。
examples.trans: Nobody is there. That is the buzzer from room four.

meanings.note: Pinyin: dōu. Summarizes everything BEFORE it and always stands directly before the verb/adjective (我们都喜欢).

examples.text: 谢谢！我们平时都直接叫名字吗？
examples.trans: Thank you! Do we usually just call each other by name here?

examples.text: 小美跟这条街上所有人说话都像老朋友。
examples.trans: Mei talks to everyone on this street like old friends.

meanings.note: Pinyin: lǐ. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 里面 ('the inside').

examples.text: 在抽屉里。我们这儿用这个大纸本子和铅笔。
examples.trans: In the drawer. Here we use this big paper ledger and a pencil.

examples.text: 在您的外套口袋里吗？
examples.trans: Are they in your coat pocket?
